title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Varying ligand substituents changes electronic effects and steric hindrance around rare-earth ions, which tunes coordination symmetry and polarizability and thereby macroscopic optical or magnetic properties.
explanation: The review treats side-chain modification and coordination expansion as the first step of structure–property engineering. Silicon substituents of different bulk on cyclooctene ligands are used to adjust the Er(III) easy-axis versus the Er–Er vector and intramolecular dipole interactions in single-molecule magnets. A separate stepwise ligand-exchange route switches rigid and flexible ligands, lowers local symmetry, and raises photoluminescence quantum yield.
scope: Rare-earth coordination complexes whose properties are set by the first coordination sphere, including Er(III) organometallic SMMs and luminescent complexes accessed by ligand exchange.
conditions: Substituent steric series on COT for Er(III); stepwise exchange between rigid and flexible ligands.
caveats: Each outcome is illustrated by a 2025 case rather than a quantified general scaling law.
